fact: The JSC's IECMS, begun in 2022 with the first paperless court, has been extended to the Constitutional Court, Supreme Court, Labour Court and all divisions of the High Court, per JSC deputy secretary Katsande.
The JSC is rolling IECMS out to Magistrates' Courts in Midlands and Mashonaland West from 1 October 2026 (Phase 4.4), with Harare and Bulawayo planned by year-end.

The Minister of State for Midlands and the JSC say IECMS includes electronic filing so litigants and legal practitioners can file documents electronically, with e-filing offices and internet hubs set up to help users.
The Minister says IECMS incorporates case tracking for litigants, and the JSC says court users can monitor cases electronically.

The Ministry of Justice's Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS) was introduced in the Chipinge and Chimanimani districts on 13 January 2026, with all court records kept in digital form, per Post On Sunday.

The Judicial Service Commission has held awareness meetings in eight provinces on its Integrated Electronic Case Management System, which its secretary says will launch on 31 December 2026 and be fully operational from 1 January.

Masvingo Mirror reports Chief Justice Gwaunza launched Phase 4.3 of the IECMS in Mashonaland East and Manicaland, extending it to 16 magistrates' courts after four other provinces, with proceedings electronically recorded and transcribed.
The rollout enables electronic filing of cases and online case tracking for litigants and legal practitioners, said Chief Justice Gwaunza.

CITE reports Deputy Chief Justice Gwaunza saying the IECMS has been in use since May 2022 in the Constitutional, Supreme and High Courts' divisions and the Labour and Administrative Courts, with 23,623 users by January 2024.
From the first paperless court's commissioning on 6 May 2022, filing of court documents and processes became electronic, and the speech says filing improved after November 2023.

The Parliamentary Legal Committee's report says the Judicial Service Commission's Integrated Electronic Case Management System, adopted in February 2022, is in use in the High Court and Superior Courts, but not yet in the Magistrates Courts.
Under Statutory Instrument 153 of 2023, High Court litigants file and serve pleadings, notices and orders electronically on the IECMS platform, which the committee reported as adverse.
